title: inbuf zeroized even on copy_from_user failure in KEY_IMPORT — key material cannot be left pending
description: In ioctl_key_import(), if copy_from_user() fails (bad ioctl struct pointer), the handler acquires the lock and calls inbuf_clear() before returning -EFAULT (lines 1625-1629). The key bytes were already written to inbuf via a prior write() syscall. Without this inbuf_clear(), the key bytes would persist in inbuf until the fd is closed — across potentially many subsequent operations. A FIPS 140-3 requirement is that CSPs not persist beyond their operational need; failing to zeroize here leaves key material in a live kernel allocation. A reviewer might say 'the copy_from_user failed, just return -EFAULT — the fd will be closed eventually' — 'eventually' is not acceptable for key material in kernel memory. The zeroize-on-all-paths discipline applies even to error paths that precede the crypto operation.
close_reason: Correct behavior: inbuf is zeroized even on copy_from_user failure because inbuf may hold partial key material written by a prior write() call. Zeroizing on all failure paths (including copy_from_user failures) prevents stale key material from persisting in heap.
